headline: Critical PHP Vulnerabilities force EU and Canada government sites offline
summary: Two major flaws in the widely-used programming language were recently discovered, prompting governments to take websites offline as a precaution.
details: Governments in the Netherlands, Denmark, France, and Finland have taken down some of their websites in response to two critical vulnerabilities discovered in the PHP programming language. Canada's Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation also confirmed the decision to go offline.

PHP is a fundamental programming language used by many major web publishing services, including WordPress and Drupal. Cybersecurity firms, using AI tools, uncovered these flaws, which could allow hackers to infiltrate and potentially control systems running PHP.

The PHP Foundation has issued a security release to patch these vulnerabilities. However, the scale of the issue is significant, with experts stating that all servers using PHP versions released in the last 20 years are potentially vulnerable, impacting a majority of the internet.
The US Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency is encouraging organizations to update to the new patch. The White House acknowledged awareness of the issue on Friday.
caption:
Critical PHP vulnerabilities have led to government websites across the EU and Canada being taken offline. The flaws could impact the majority of the internet.

Governments in the Netherlands, Denmark, France, and Finland have taken down some of their websites in response to two critical vulnerabilities discovered in the PHP programming language. Canada's Minister of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Innovation also confirmed the decision to go offline.

PHP is a fundamental programming language used by many major web publishing services, including WordPress and Drupal. Cybersecurity firms, using AI tools, uncovered these flaws, which could allow hackers to infiltrate and potentially control systems running PHP.

The PHP Foundation has issued a security release to patch these vulnerabilities. However, the scale of the issue is significant, with experts stating that all servers using PHP versions released in the last 20 years are potentially vulnerable, impacting a majority of the internet.

The US Cybersecurity & Infrastructure Security Agency is encouraging organizations to update to the new patch. The White House acknowledged awareness of the issue on Friday.
